Scrum Guide 2020: "Scrum defines three specific accountabilities within the Scrum Team: the Developers, the Product Owner, and the Scrum Master." and "All the work necessary to achieve the Product Goal, including Sprint Planning, Daily Scrums, Sprint Review, and Sprint Retrospective, happen within Sprints." (the Sprint plus four events). Artifacts: "The Product Backlog is an emergent, ordered list...", "The Sprint Backlog is composed of the Sprint Goal (why)...", "Multiple Increments may be created within a Sprint."
claim_verdicts.source: https://scrumguides.org/scrum-guide.html (2020 edition), Scrum Team / Scrum Events / Scrum Artifacts

claim_verdicts.evidence: Scrum Guide 2020: "They are fixed length events of one month or less to create consistency. A new Sprint starts immediately after the conclusion of the previous Sprint." and the events sentence quoted at claim 8. The Guide states no cut-the-work rule; the nearest is "Scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned." The claim's own caveat (implication, not a stated rule) is therefore correct — but the lesson body states it flatly (see issue, section 3).

Scrum Guide 2020: PO Product Backlog management includes "Ordering Product Backlog items"; Developers: "The Developers who will be doing the work are responsible for the sizing." and Sprint Planning Topic Three "How will the chosen work get done?"; Scrum Master serves by "Causing the removal of impediments to the Scrum Team's progress". The Guide never calls the Scrum Master a manager and says "Within a Scrum Team, there are no sub-teams or hierarchies."
claim_verdicts.source: https://scrumguides.org/scrum-guide.html — Product Owner / Developers / Scrum Master

claim_verdicts.evidence: Scrum Guide 2020: "In order to provide value, the Increment must be usable."; "Work cannot be considered part of an Increment unless it meets the Definition of Done."; "If a Product Backlog item does not meet the Definition of Done, it cannot be released or even presented at the Sprint Review."; "Multiple Increments may be created within a Sprint." All four parts of the claim are carried.
claim_verdicts.source: https://scrumguides.org/scrum-guide.html — Increment / Commitment: Definition of Done

claim_verdicts.evidence: Scrum Guide 2020: "The Daily Scrum is a 15-minute event for the Developers of the Scrum Team. To reduce complexity, it is held at the same time and place every working day of the Sprint." and "The purpose of the Daily Scrum is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary, adjusting the upcoming planned work." The Guide adds 'and place', which the claim and the lesson omit — harmless.

Scrum Guide 2020, Sprint Review: "The Scrum Team presents the results of their work to key stakeholders" and "The Product Backlog may also be adjusted to meet new opportunities." Retrospective: "The Scrum Team inspects how the last Sprint went with regards to individuals, interactions, processes, tools, and their Definition of Done." and "The most impactful improvements are addressed as soon as possible." No count of changes appears anywhere — the claim's 'No number is prescribed' holds, and the body contradicts it (see issue, section 3).

No tester role appears in the Scrum Guide 2020, and "The Developers who will be doing the work are responsible for the sizing." with no unit named — both halves hold. But the Guide is not silent on a separate tester: "Within a Scrum Team, there are no sub-teams or hierarchies." and Developers are the people "committed to creating any usable aspect of a usable Increment each Sprint". A person who tests but is 'not counted among the developers' sits outside a structure the Guide does define.
claim_verdicts.source: https://scrumguides.org/scrum-guide.html — Scrum Team / Developers / Product Backlog
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: The reference names no tester and no specialist roles at all: everyone doing the work is a developer, and it forbids sub-teams inside the team. It makes the developers responsible for sizing without naming a unit, so a number against each piece of work is one permitted way of sizing.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Scrum Guide 2020: "The purpose of the Daily Scrum is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary, adjusting the upcoming planned work." — the meeting exists to change the plan, so the sentence that changes a plan is the one it is for. The note independently marks it: "Câu thứ ba là câu quan trọng nhất."

Scrum Guide 2020: "Changing the core design or ideas of Scrum, leaving out elements, or not following the rules of Scrum, covers up problems and limits the benefits of Scrum." and "While implementing only parts of Scrum is possible, the result is not Scrum." Both halves of the claim are carried as written.

Definitional: if the end date is moved whenever the work is late, there is no date fixed in advance left to compare the outcome against, so 'slow' and 'badly estimated' cannot be told apart. Consonant with the Guide's "They are fixed length events of one month or less to create consistency", which is the only thing the Guide says on the point; no source asserts the diagnostic consequence and none is needed.

Definitional: a local variant can only be told apart from the reference by someone who knows the reference. The substantive half — which changes leave elements out — is claim 17 and is sourced there ("leaving out elements ... covers up problems and limits the benefits of Scrum"). Nothing here is a behaviour, number or syntax statement.
Scrum Guide 2020, Sprint Review: "The Sprint Review is a working session and the Scrum Team should avoid limiting it to a presentation." Exactly the claim.

The document at scrumguides.org is titled 'The 2020 Scrum Guide™' (November 2020) and the site states it is "written and provided by" Ken Schwaber and Jeff Sutherland and "contains the definition of Scrum" including "accountabilities, events, artifacts, and the rules that bind them together". It is the reference description, and it is called the Scrum Guide.

issues.quote: the two backlogs — the product backlog is everything wanted, kept in order; the sprint backlog is the goal, the slice this sprint took to serve it, and the team's plan for both
issues.text: Unlisted claim: the composition of both backlogs. The ledger's claim 8 only names the three artifacts; nothing in it covers what a product backlog or a sprint backlog contains, yet these are specific, checkable assertions about the reference. Both happen to be right, so this is a ledger defect, not a content defect.
issues.fix: Add a claim: 'In the reference the product backlog is an emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product; the sprint backlog is composed of the sprint goal (why), the items selected for the sprint (what) and an actionable plan for delivering the increment (how).' source_hint: Scrum Guide 2020, sections Product Backlog and Sprint Backlog; version_key scrum.

issues.quote: the retrospective (change one thing about how the team works)
issues.text: The reference prescribes no number of changes — "The most impactful improvements are addressed as soon as possible" — and claim 13 says so in the ledger ('No number is prescribed'). Yet Core concepts, the diagram box 'Retrospective: change one thing', section 4 ('one change to try') and summary line 5 all state the one-thing rule inside material the lesson presents as the Guide summarised. The body contradicts its own claim.
issues.fix: Keep the number only where it describes this team. Core concepts: 'the retrospective (decide what to change in how the team works)'. Diagram: 'Retrospective: decide what to change'. Section 4: 'what to keep, what hurt, what to change — this team picked one thing.' Summary line 5 needs no change.

issues.quote: That standard here includes conditions written down before coding and a second person reading the code.
issues.text: Misdescribes the source note. The note records the conditions-before-coding item under 'Làm tốt' (what worked), not as the agreed standard, and the second reader is 'Hành động cho sprint sau: mỗi việc lớn hơn 3 điểm phải có hai người đọc code' — an action for the NEXT sprint, limited to items above 3. The lesson presents both as the standard already in force for all work, which the note does not say.
issues.fix: Replace with: 'The team's retrospective names what feeds that standard: writing the conditions down before coding worked, and from the next sprint anything sized above three gets a second person reading the code.' Then delete the duplicate mention in the closing paragraph of section 5 or keep only one of the two.

issues.quote: A team that wants work to flow with no fixed length gives up the sprint on purpose: a different method, not a broken one.
issues.text: Unlisted claim. Claim 15 was withdrawn and no remaining claim covers this sentence, yet it makes two assertions about the reference: that dropping the fixed length removes the sprint, and that the result is a legitimate different method rather than broken Scrum. Both need a source.
issues.fix: Add a claim resting on the Guide's "While implementing only parts of Scrum is possible, the result is not Scrum." and reword to match it: '… gives up the sprint on purpose; by the reference's own words the result is then not Scrum, which is a choice, not a fault.'

issues.quote: the team demonstrates on a machine the whole team can reach, not on one person's own
issues.text: The note says 'trên môi trường thử nghiệm, không phải trên máy cá nhân' — a test environment, not 'a machine the whole team can reach'. Reachability is not what the note contrasts; a personal machine can be reachable. The quiz explanation for q2 option b already says 'a shared test environment', so lesson and quiz disagree on the same line.
issues.fix: Write: 'the team demonstrates on a shared test environment, not on one person's own machine'.

issues.quote: it has a tester as a separate person, which the Guide does not name
issues.text: True that no tester is named, but the Guide is not silent here: "Within a Scrum Team, there are no sub-teams or hierarchies", and the Developers are the people committed to creating any usable aspect of the increment. Presenting a person outside the four developers as something the reference simply does not mention overstates the silence.
issues.fix: Write: 'it has a tester as a separate person, where the reference names no specialist roles at all — everyone doing the work is a developer'. Keep the verdict (still an ordinary adaptation), and apply the same wording to quiz q6 option a.

issues.quote: a time box — a duration decided before the work starts; when the work does not fit, the work is cut, not the duration
issues.text: Stated as part of the reference summary, but the Guide states only "They are fixed length events of one month or less" plus "Scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned." There is no cut-the-work rule in the text; claim 9 admits this is an implication, the body does not.
issues.fix: Attribute the second half instead of asserting it: 'a time box — a duration decided before the work starts and not changed afterwards, so when the work does not fit, what moves is the work, as this team's note shows.'

issues.quote: the four meetings inside a sprint — planning (what and how)
issues.text: Sprint Planning has three topics in the reference — Topic One "Why is this Sprint valuable?", Topic Two "What can be Done this Sprint?", Topic Three "How will the chosen work get done?". The lesson's own section 4 makes the goal the first thing planning produces, so the two-word gloss is narrower than both the Guide and the rest of the lesson.
issues.fix: Write 'planning (why, what and how)'.

issues.quote: the result is the sprint backlog, which the team itself owns and rearranges as it learns
issues.text: The reference says "The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers", and the Developers are accountable for "Adapting their plan each day toward the Sprint Goal". Ownership is the developers', not the whole team's; the lesson elsewhere keeps that distinction (the daily is 'the developers talking to each other').
issues.fix: Write: 'which the developers own and rearrange as they learn'.

issues.quote: The sprint, the three roles, the two backlogs and the four meetings above are what the word Scrum names
issues.text: Not exhaustive: the reference also names the product goal, the sprint goal and the definition of done as commitments attached to the three artifacts, plus five values. Claiming the list is what the word names invites a junior to treat anything else heard at work as non-Scrum.
issues.fix: Write: 'The sprint, the three roles, the two backlogs and the four meetings above are the parts of Scrum this lesson covers; the reference describes these and a few more.'

issues.quote: Three roles (product owner, scrum master, developers), five events ... and three artifacts ... — and what each one asks of you specifically.
issues.text: Outline item 2's second half is delivered for the daily (say what blocks you) and for the review (do not show unfinished work), but not for planning, the retrospective or the two backlogs: the lesson says what they are, never what a junior is expected to do in them.
issues.fix: Add one clause each in section 4: at planning you say whether the slice fits the days you have; at the retrospective you bring one thing that cost you time; on the sprint backlog you move your own row and do not wait to be asked.

issues.quote: versions_used: [scrum]
issues.text: content/versions.yaml pins no edition for `scrum` (only `docs: https://scrumguides.org/`), yet the lesson is edition-specific: 'accountabilities' for the three roles, five events and three artifacts are the 2020 wording, and the 2017 edition said 'roles' and had a different retrospective text. Nothing would force a re-review if the site published a new edition.
issues.fix: Add `version: "2020"` and `checked: 2026-09-22` under `standards.scrum` in content/versions.yaml, leaving the body unchanged; the versions.yaml policy line then makes any new edition trigger a re-review of this lesson.

issues.quote: One person on the team only tests, and is not counted among the four developers.
issues.text: Keyed correct, and correct given the lesson text as it stands. But 'not counted among the four developers' is precisely the part the reference does address ("Within a Scrum Team, there are no sub-teams or hierarchies"), so the option is only safe while the lesson keeps its overstated 'the Guide does not name' framing. Answer key a+b is otherwise right: b, c, d and e all resolve as the lesson resolves them.
issues.fix: Reword option a to 'One person on the team works only on testing, and the team calls that person a tester', and keep it in the key; make the same change in the lesson sentence in section 5.

issues.text: A way of working with no fixed length turns up here for the first and last time, inside half a sentence. Nothing tells me what "work to flow" is or how a team runs without sprints; the prereq gave me two shapes only, everything at once or small slices, and this is a third. It appears in no other section, no summary line and no quiz question, so I stopped over something I never use.
issues.fix: Delete the clause: end the paragraph at "…covers up problems and limits the benefits." If the point must stay, write instead: "A team that drops the fixed length on purpose is, by the reference's own words, no longer doing Scrum — a choice rather than a fault."

issues.text: Section 5 says the reference "permits [sizing] without naming a unit"; it never says this team chose a unit, and the table shows a bare number with no unit written anywhere. So I could not decide whether option b restates the lesson's second difference or adds a claim the lesson does not make. On a select-all question that doubt costs the whole item.

issues.text: "The ones" has no noun in front of it. The sentence before ends on "leaves the parts listed in Core concepts in place", so my first guess was "the parts", which makes the sentence say the opposite of what it means. I read back twice before working out it means other adaptations.

issues.text: This sits between the diagram and the prose that walks me through the diagram. I had just read seven boxes and wanted the walkthrough; instead I got a document I have not read and the word "accountabilities", which is explained only by standing next to "roles" and never used again.
issues.fix: Move this sentence to the end of section 4, after "…the next sprint opens on the reordered backlog", and drop ", and calls the roles accountabilities".

issues.text: The only meaning of "commit" I have been taught is the Git one: a snapshot with an id, author, message and parent. "commits to one goal" uses the word in a different sense that is never signalled, and on first reading I looked for a Git action. The same wording repeats in section 4, summary line 1 and quiz q4.
issues.fix: In the `sprint` bullet write "in which the team promises itself one goal", and use the same verb in section 4 ("the team picks a goal it can promise") and summary line 1.

issues.text: In the diagram the daily is one box in a left-to-right chain, so on first read it looks like something that happens once between the sprint backlog and the increment. issues.text: Section 4 says "The retrospective is the one meeting about the team rather than the product". issues.text: Six bullets carry about twelve named things, and only `sprint` is marked. When section 5 sent me back to check what a product backlog is, I had to scan inside a bullet whose label is "the two backlogs" and find the clause before the semicolon. issues.fix: Inside each bullet, put the named thing first and its meaning after a dash, e.g. "the two backlogs — the product backlog: everything wanted, kept in order; the sprint backlog: the goal, the slice this sprint took, and the plan for both".
